title: EXP-126 - Hello World Part 8 Phase 7: Add To Cart Event Pipeline (FX_SetNewCartEntry Set Values, FX_AddToCart Make Current/New/Generate Event) and Drag From/Drop On Wiring on FX_CustomerPortal, with a Close/Reopen Readback
objective: Do Hello World Part 8 Phase 7 (16:54-21:04) in the Designer on FX_CustomerPortal (User scope): create the handler FX_SetNewCartEntry (the tutorial's 'Set New Cart Entry'), Response Type Set Values with three property pairs on the primary collection (FX_Orders): FX_Item = the secondary collection's FX_Item (Property Value), FX_Count = V(FX_Count), FX_CustomerID = V(FX_CustomerID); create the handler group FX_AddToCart (the tutorial's 'Add To Cart') with three rows in order: Collection Make Current on the primary collection, Collection New on the primary collection, Generate Event FX_SetNewCartEntry with Post Event Asynchronously; add FX_AddToCart to GridItems' Drag From Events and to ButtonAddToCart's Drop On Events; read everything back after one Designer close/reopen. T1 gate; T2 FX_SetNewCartEntry with the FX_Item pair; T3 the FX_Count and FX_CustomerID pairs; T4 to T6 one FX_AddToCart row each; T7 GridItems Drag From Events; T8 ButtonAddToCart Drop On Events; T9 readback and final audit. Designer only: no runtime action (the drag test and checkout are Phase 8). Findings are observed only.

in_scope: Before browser interaction read AGENTS.md (the repository file, at the start of every task), docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt8.md 'Instructions for AI agents' (lines 12-22), Phase 7 (lines 188-211) and transcript lines 474-513 (16:54-21:04), recipes/session/session-expiry-and-stale-designer.md, and only the final Outcome (operator) sections of the EXP-125, EXP-124, EXP-123 and EXP-117 records. Read nothing else: no other records and no later Part 8 phases. In a continuation task, AGENTS.md and the current task's part of this record are enough.
Create or update only experiments/EXP-126-hello-world-part-8-phase-7-add-to-cart-handlers-drag-drop.md and evidence/EXP-126/ documentation and evidence files.
Record the worker-written-file inventory and a cumulative browser action audit with exact counts.

Use the existing authenticated session without refresh, restart or configuration change. If a session expiry, logout card or sign-in page appears, record it and stop for the operator (EXP-107: the operator signs in manually); do not navigate, type credentials or screenshot a filled sign-in form. List the browser tabs before the first tab selection. Answer any prompt within the same task; never leave a prompt, dialog, menu or unsaved change open across tasks. After any pause, inspect the state read-only before acting and never replay an earlier action. Signed-out session (EXP-116): a server-event error together with a portal tab reading 'Logout Successful' means the session ended; record it and stop for the operator.

Task boundary: do only what the current task instruction lists and stop at its end, even when later steps of this brief remain; report the next step instead of performing it. Turn budget (EXP-109, EXP-111): if a task cannot finish, stop only at a step boundary right after a Save (never with an unsaved change, open list, editor or dialog) and report the next step.

Server-event rule (EXP-103-R2 lesson): if any action raises 'The server event processing returned an error', answer OK once, record it and stop blocked for an operator Designer reload; never try another route, retry, close or reopen after that error. Console-error stop (EXP-110-R2 lesson: a Caption commit can fail silently with HTTP 400 and surface only at the next server event): record the page console error count shown in the browser tool output at the start of each task and after every action in T1 to T9 (Designer tab; record the Web Client count once in T1); if it rises after any action, record the action and the counts and stop blocked before any further click (no ellipsis, no Save, no close), leaving the state for the operator. Never read or inspect the console messages themselves. A rise can also come from a client-side Designer script error (EXP-111 T5: an uncaught TypeError at a component selection); the stop rule is the same, and the operator diagnoses the cause from the tool-written console log. A Caption commit that leaves Save disabled is also a stop signal (EXP-110-R2): record it and stop blocked before any further click.

Editing scope: stay in User scope throughout. If an 'Identify Your Editing Scope' dialog appears, confirm it shows User for the signed-in user and accept it unchanged; if it shows any other scope, Cancel it and stop blocked.

Gate (T1, read-only): list the tabs; identify the Web Client (portal app) and Web Designer tabs. Web Client: record which runtime Form (if any) is open and whether it has unsaved changes (if so, record it and stop for the operator) and its console error count; change nothing there. Designer: User scope; FX_CustomerPortal open and clean (Save disabled), no dialog open; if another Form tab is active, select FX_CustomerPortal's tab; if it is not open, open it once through the Form menu recent-forms entry (never Select Form OK). Record: Details > Event Handlers (every group and row; expected StdFormPredisplay; FX_SignInBtn with Collection Refresh then Set Values SETVARVALUES(FX_Page=2); FX_SignInBtn2, FX_HomeBtn, FX_CartBtn; if a group named FX_SetNewCartEntry or FX_AddToCart exists, record it and stop blocked); Details > Variables (expected FX_Count, FX_CustomerID and FX_Page under Form - Temporary); Details > Collections or the Form's collection properties if shown without opening a dialog (expected primary FX_Orders, secondary collection 2 FX_Items; record what is shown). Then select GridItems (FlexLayoutMain > Region03: homepage) and ButtonAddToCart (FlexLayoutButtons) by their Components row Type cell, confirm the Properties header names each, and record their Events group rows (expected rows Drag From Events and Drop On Events, both blank; if either already holds a value, record it and stop blocked). Expanding groups is view only (a group expands on a label double-click, EXP-122); open no ellipsis or list. Verify Save is still disabled. Record the Designer baseline console error count. Screenshots: the Event Handlers tab; GridItems' Events group.

Efficiency rules (operator, 2026-10-16): screenshots only for the decisive states named in this brief; do not re-open saved images unless a decision needs it; one untargeted snapshot per step; read only the named sources; never search or read the worker's own session transcript. Use inline untargeted snapshots; never save snapshots to files and Grep them (EXP-109 ran out of turns that way). Lists (EXP-111 lesson): choose a list option by clicking it; never pick options with arrow keys, Enter or Tab while a list is open, because Tab commits the highlighted item. Stale references (operator ruling, EXP-111): the allowance is one fresh untargeted snapshot per 'Ref not found' error, not one per task. Snapshot size (EXP-114): if an untargeted snapshot is too large to return inline, take targeted snapshots of the needed panel instead (record that); never save snapshots to files.

Property rules (EXP-055, EXP-056, EXP-111, EXP-120): select a component by its Components row (click its Type cell) and confirm the Properties header names it. Lists: open the list with its arrow and click the planned option, then leave the field by clicking a neutral row (never Tab or arrow keys while a list is open); if the planned option is absent, close the list without choosing and stop blocked before any OK or Save. Text fields: click the value cell, one plain fill, one Tab; verify. At most one correction per field. Record the console error count after each action. After each performed step exactly one Designer Save, recording its response and the Save state. Answer an OK-only informational prompt with OK and record it verbatim; any other prompt not covered here: record it, choose the non-changing answer (No or Cancel) and stop blocked. Close every nested dialog you opened with its OK (planned change) or Cancel (no change), innermost first; never leave one open across tasks.

Handler creation (EXP-123, EXP-124 routes; every handler row is created with New, never with the handler Copy button): Details > Event Handlers > New (+) once; the Event Handler dialog's Name field is pre-filled with the previous name (EXP-124): clear it (one Control+A, then type) and type the task's handler name key by key; record the dialog, then OK once; record the new group and row with its sequence number. Select the new row by its Response Type cell. Set Response Type ONLY in the lower Properties grid (EXP-124 finding 1): expand all, open the Response > Type sub-row arrow and click the planned type (the grid's Response Type cell offers no list). Then open the Parameters ellipsis once (Event Handler Parameters dialog) and record its fields before acting. If the planned type or a planned option is not offered, close the list without choosing, Cancel every dialog you opened and stop blocked before any Save. New with an existing name appends the next sequence row to that group with no prompt (EXP-124 finding 2); if a prompt appears, record it verbatim and answer with the non-changing choice; if a new row replaces or reorders an existing row, or lands in another group, record it and stop blocked before any further change or Save.

FX_SetNewCartEntry (T2 and T3; tutorial 17:06-18:54). T2: create the handler FX_SetNewCartEntry (Handler creation rule), Response Type Set Values; in Event Handler Parameters open the Properties ellipsis once (an 'Edit Set Property Values' list, expected empty; record its title and controls), New once (a property pair dialog; record its fields: expected a Target property and a collection for the target, and a Value with an ellipsis). Target: choose FX_Item from the property list; leave the collection for the target at the primary collection (FX_Orders; record how it is named; if it names another collection and offers the primary one, click the primary one; otherwise stop blocked). Value: click the Value ellipsis once; in the value dialog set Value Type Property Value (click it in the list), the collection to the secondary collection (it may be named by slot, e.g. 'secondary collection 2', EXP-117; record every collection option) and the property FX_Item (click it in the list; never another property); OK. Record the pair text the dialog shows (the tutorial says a 2 prefix marks the secondary collection). OK on the pair dialog, the list, and Event Handler Parameters. Verify and record the handler row's Response Parameters text. One Designer Save. Screenshots: the value dialog before its OK; the pair dialog before its OK; the handler row before the Save; the Save response state. T3: select the FX_SetNewCartEntry row; open its Parameters ellipsis and then the Properties ellipsis once (record that the list holds the FX_Item pair); New once: Target FX_Count (primary collection), Value: click the value textbox and type V(FX_Count) key by key, then Tab; OK. New once more: Target FX_CustomerID (primary collection), Value V(FX_CustomerID) typed the same way; OK. Verify the list holds the three pairs in this order and the FX_Item pair is unchanged; OK on the list and Event Handler Parameters. Verify and record the handler row's Response Parameters text. One Designer Save. Screenshots: the list with three pairs before its OK; the handler row before the Save; the Save response state.

FX_AddToCart (T4 to T6, one row per task; tutorial 18:54-19:56). T4: create the handler FX_AddToCart, Response Type Collection Make Current; Parameters: the collection set to the primary collection (FX_Orders; record every collection option and how the primary one is named); OK; record the row's Response Parameters; one Designer Save. T5: New with the name FX_AddToCart (expected a sequence 1 row in the FX_AddToCart group), Response Type Collection New; Parameters: the primary collection, as in T4; OK; record; one Designer Save. T6: New with the name FX_AddToCart (expected sequence 2), Response Type Generate Event; Parameters: choose the event FX_SetNewCartEntry (click it in its list; if it must be typed, type FX_SetNewCartEntry key by key and Tab), and check the Post Event Asynchronously box (record its exact label; if no such option exists, record the dialog, Cancel and stop blocked); leave every other field at its default; OK; record the row's Response Parameters; verify all three FX_AddToCart rows in sequence order 0 Make Current, 1 New, 2 Generate Event; one Designer Save. Screenshots per task: the Parameters dialog before its OK; the FX_AddToCart group before the Save; the Save response state.

Drag and drop wiring (T7 GridItems Drag From Events; T8 ButtonAddToCart Drop On Events; tutorial 20:21-20:59): select the task's component by its Components row Type cell and confirm the Properties header; in its Events group click the planned row's ellipsis once and record the dialog (title, lists, buttons) with a screenshot before acting. Expected: a list of events, an Add button and OK. Click FX_AddToCart in the event list (never another event), click Add once, verify FX_AddToCart is listed as added, then OK. If FX_AddToCart is not offered, Cancel and stop blocked. Verify and record the row's value; one Designer Save. Screenshots per task: the dialog at open; the dialog before its OK; the Events group before the Save; the Save response state.

Readback and audit (T9, one task): close the clean FX_CustomerPortal once through its Form-tab control (answer No to any save prompt, record its text), reopen it once through the Form menu recent-forms entry, and read: Details > Event Handlers (every group and row: FX_SetNewCartEntry Set Values with its Response Parameters; FX_AddToCart rows 0 Collection Make Current, 1 Collection New, 2 Generate Event, with their Response Parameters; the earlier groups unchanged); GridItems Drag From Events and ButtonAddToCart Drop On Events (FX_AddToCart each). Open no dialog or list. Leave FX_CustomerPortal open and clean. Then, in the same task, write the documentation-only final audit into the record: decisive evidence for each acceptance check, the cumulative action audit with exact counts, the worker-written-file inventory, the cleanup inventory and the final state. Screenshots: Event Handlers with both new groups; GridItems' Events group; ButtonAddToCart's Events group.

Before every click, use references from the most recent snapshot taken in the current task (not from find output); after any timeout or 'Ref not found', take one fresh untargeted snapshot and use only its references (one per error). ExtJS comboboxes are not <select> elements (EXP-101): open their list and click the option. Coordinates are allowed only once per field for a list arrow that has no reference (EXP-111: a value-cell double-click may expose it first); record each such click. Record any blocker after at most one fresh untargeted snapshot and one corrected visible inspection; never leave a prompt, list, editor or dialog open across tasks. Classify findings as observed only.

initial_instruction: T1 - Read-only gate for EXP-126. First read the repository file AGENTS.md, then hello-world-pt8.md lines 12-22 and 188-211 and transcript lines 474-513, recipes/session/session-expiry-and-stale-designer.md, and only the Outcome (operator) sections of EXP-125, EXP-124, EXP-123 and EXP-117, all before any browser action; read nothing else. Without shell/git access, record the starting state concisely. List the browser tabs before selecting one; identify the Web Client and Web Designer tabs. If either shows a session expiry, logout card, 'Logout Successful' or sign-in, record it and stop for the operator (do not sign in, do not click OK on a Session Expired message; never screenshot a filled sign-in form). Record each tab's console error count shown in the tool output (do not read the messages); if it rises after any action, record the action and stop. In the Web Client record which runtime Form is open and whether it has unsaved changes (if so, stop for the operator); change nothing there. In the Designer confirm User scope, that FX_CustomerPortal is open and clean (select its Form tab if another is active; open it once through the Form menu recent-forms entry only if it is not open) and that no dialog is open. If any action raises the server-event error, answer OK once, record it and stop. Record Details > Event Handlers (StdFormPredisplay, FX_SignInBtn with two rows, FX_SignInBtn2, FX_HomeBtn, FX_CartBtn expected; stop blocked if FX_SetNewCartEntry or FX_AddToCart exists) and Details > Variables (FX_Count, FX_CustomerID, FX_Page expected). Select by Components row Type cell and record, for GridItems and ButtonAddToCart, the Events group rows (Drag From Events and Drop On Events expected blank; if not blank, record it and stop blocked). Open no ellipsis or list; verify Save is still disabled. Screenshots: Event Handlers; GridItems' Events group. Use inline snapshots only (targeted panel snapshots if an untargeted one is too large). Make no change in T1. This is the end of T1 even though later brief steps remain. Create the EXP-126 record with the gate, the readings, the action audit and the file inventory, with screenshots under evidence/EXP-126/ (distinct filenames), and stop with no menu, dialog or list open.
